facility_roles.quote: experiment was located on La Palma (Canary Islands) at a height of 2200 m a.s.l. (at the site of the Observatory operated by the IAC).

intervals.label: data taking
intervals.note: The official page dates data taking with the various detector types to 1987-2002. Individual instruments started later: the first imaging telescope's camera in mid-1992 and AIROBICC in 1992 (arXiv:2406.15037); the five-telescope stereoscopic system was completed in 1997.
intervals.quote: With its various types of detectors HEGRA was taking data between 1987 and 2002.

intervals.label: data taking ended
intervals.note: The Cherenkov telescopes were dismantled in September 2002 (same page).
intervals.quote: With its various types of detectors HEGRA was taking data between 1987 and 2002.

quantity.quote: at a height of 2200 m a.s.l.
There were a total of six of these telescopes in operation.
More than 250 of these counters were in operation, spread over a 180-by-180 m2 area.
The system provides a gamma-ray energy threshold around 0.5 TeV.

website.note: Archive page kept by the Max-Planck-Institut fuer Kernphysik; the original HEGRA server in Hamburg is offline.

name: HEGRA
notes: Successors: the official page names MAGIC (at the HEGRA site) and H.E.S.S.; the lineage rows (predecessor) are on experiment:magic and experiment:h-e-s-s.
The telescope count is six on the official page (the stereoscopic system proper had five identical telescopes plus the first telescope, CT1).
No INSPIRE experiment id is recorded: INSPIRE was not contacted by this stream.

physics_goals.quote: One of the major aims of the HEGRA ex- periment is the search for galactic and extra- galactic sources of TeV γ-radiation
physics_goals.value: Search for galactic and extragalactic TeV gamma-ray sources with stereoscopic imaging Cherenkov telescopes, and study cosmic-ray spectra and composition with the air-shower arrays.

summary.plain: A cluster of cosmic-ray and gamma-ray detectors on the mountaintop of La Palma that ran from 1987 to 2002. Its team of stereoscopic Cherenkov telescopes demonstrated the advantages of stereoscopic observation, continued by its successors MAGIC and H.E.S.S.
summary.technical: HEGRA (High Energy Gamma Ray Astronomy) at the Roque de los Muchachos, 2200 m: a system of five to six imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (threshold about 0.5 TeV) plus the AIROBICC Cherenkov counters, a scintillator array and muon towers. Data taking 1987-2002; successors MAGIC (same site) and H.E.S.S.

unique_capabilities.quote: It demonstrated the advantages of stereo observations as the strong background suppression and hence the increased sensitivity
unique_capabilities.value: A stereoscopic system of imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes: stereo observation gives strong background suppression, higher sensitivity and better energy and angular resolution than a single telescope.
